questions.q: How does SAQL differ in structure from SQL and SOQL?
options: It is a sequence of statements that pass streams from one to the next
It uses no keywords at all
It is a single statement with a fixed clause order
It can only run against Salesforce objects
questions.explain: SQL and SOQL describe the result in one statement with fixed clause order. SAQL is a pipeline where each statement's output stream feeds the next.

questions.q: What does SOQL query, compared with SAQL?
options: Live Salesforce objects, subject to Salesforce query limits
questions.explain: SOQL reads live Salesforce objects. SAQL reads prepared CRM Analytics datasets, so its results are only as fresh as the last load.

questions.q: In SAQL, how do you combine two datasets that share a field?
options: With cogroup, which groups the inputs on a shared field first
questions.explain: SAQL uses cogroup. Because the grouping happens first, it is not the same as a row-level SQL join and the original row grain is lost.

questions.q: Which SAQL statement pair replaces the SELECT-list-plus-GROUP BY of a SQL query?
questions.explain: group sets up the grouping, and foreach ... generate defines the output columns and aggregates.

questions.q: A SAQL filter placed after foreach ... generate behaves most like which SQL concept?
questions.explain: Placement matters in a SAQL pipeline: a filter before group narrows rows like WHERE, while a filter after generate filters aggregated results like HAVING.
